Sign-pattern test for the maximum of L statistics, with a sensitivity bound

Source: R/rosenbaum-pairs.R
riposte_pairs_perm_test.Rd

Under the sharp null in a paired randomized experiment, each difference's sign is equally likely to be either, independently across pairs. Under Rosenbaum's sensitivity model with hidden bias at most gamma, each sign is instead positive with some chance no larger than theta = gamma / (1 + gamma). Because the scores are nonnegative, the chance that the maximum standardized statistic reaches its observed value is largest when every sign is positive with chance theta, so that chance is an upper bound on the p-value (and the exact p-value at gamma = 1). This function computes it from the distribution of the signs: by listing every sign pattern with its chance when nresample is NULL (at most 16 pairs with nonzero difference), otherwise from nresample random patterns with the observed signs counted as one of them. riposte_pairs_bound() gives the normal approximation to the same bound.

Usage

riposte_pairs_perm_test(y, H, nresample = 9999L, gamma = 1)

Arguments

y

matched-pair differences.

H

numeric matrix, one row per pair, one column per statistic (2 <= L).

nresample

number of random sign vectors, or NULL for full enumeration (requires at most 16 nonzero pairs).

gamma

sensitivity parameter, >= 1; 1 (the default) gives the randomization test of the sharp null.

Value

a list with p.value (an upper bound when gamma > 1) and the observed statistic, the maximum of the statistics standardized at theta.

References

Rosenbaum, P. R. (2012) Testing one hypothesis twice in observational studies. Biometrika 99(4), 763-774.
